claim: Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) is essential for gene silencing.
source_text: Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) is essential for gene silencing
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established fact in the field, representing established scientific consensus about PRC2 function.

claim: PRC2 establishes transcriptional repression of specific genes by tri-methylating Lysine 27 of histone H3.
source_text: establishing transcriptional repression of specific genes by tri-methylating Lysine 27 of histone H3
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about PRC2's mechanism of action, supported by citations in the introduction (Cao et al., 2002; Czermin et al., 2002; Muller et al., 2002; Kirmizis et al., 2004).

claim: AEBP2 is a cofactor that mediates PRC2's methylation process.
source_text: a process mediated by cofactors such as AEBP2
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by established knowledge and citations about AEBP2's role as a PRC2 cofactor.

claim: This study presents the first three-dimensional electron microscopy structure of the human PRC2 complex bound to its cofactor AEBP2.
source_text: Here, we present the first three-dimensional electron microscopy structure of the human PRC2 complex bound to its cofactor AEBP2.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the experimental EM data and 3D reconstruction presented in the manuscript.

claim: A novel internal protein tagging-method was used to localize all PRC2 subunits and their functional domains.
source_text: Using a novel internal protein tagging-method, in combination with isotopic chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry, we have localized all the PRC2 subunits and their functional domains
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the experimental data from the internal GFP tagging experiments described in the Results section.

claim: The position and stabilization effect of AEBP2 suggests an allosteric role of this cofactor in regulating gene silencing.
source_text: The position and stabilization effect of AEBP2 suggests an allosteric role of this cofactor in regulating gene silencing.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the structural data showing AEBP2's position and its stabilizing effect on the complex, combined with cross-linking data.

claim: Regions in PRC2 that interact with modified histone tails are localized near the methyltransferase site.
source_text: Regions in PRC2 that interact with modified histone tails are localized near the methyltransferase site
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the structural localization data combined with docking of crystal structures showing histone binding sites.

claim: PcG and TrxG complexes are evolutionarily conserved in eukaryotes.
source_text: PcG and TrxG complexes are evolutionarily conserved in eukaryotes
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the citation (Schuettengruber et al., 2007).

claim: PRC2 plays an essential role in chromatin modification by di- and tri-methylating Lys 27 of Histone H3 (H3K27me2/3).
source_text: Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) plays an essential role in chromatin modification by di- and tri-methylating Lys 27 of Histone H3 (H3K27me2/3)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations (Cao et al., 2002; Czermin et al., 2002; Muller et al., 2002; Kirmizis et al., 2004).

claim: In higher eukaryotes, high levels of H3K27me3 are typically associated with transcriptional repression and gene silencing.
source_text: In higher eukaryotes, high levels of H3K27me3 are typically associated with transcriptional repression and gene silencing.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established scientific consensus about the function of H3K27me3 marks.

claim: Deletion of any PcG protein components in mice results in early embryonic lethality or severe defects during development.
source_text: deletion of any of its components in mice results in early embryonic lethality or severe defects during development
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to experimental studies (O'Carroll et al., 2001; Pasini et al., 2004).

claim: PRC2 co-purifies with the protein AEBP2.
source_text: Biochemical studies have shown that PRC2 co-purifies with the protein AEBP2
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies (Cao and Zhang, 2004b; Kim et al., 2009).

claim: AEBP2 interaction aids in targeting of PRC2 to specific DNA sites and enhances its methyl-transferase activity.
source_text: it has been proposed that this interaction aids in targeting of PRC2 to specific DNA sites and enhances its methyl-transferase activity
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Cao and Zhang, 2004b; Kim et al., 2009) describing proposed mechanisms.

claim: AEBP2 is present in two isoforms in humans: an adult-specific larger form (51 kDa) and an embryo-specific smaller form (32 kDa).
source_text: This important cofactor is an evolutionarily conserved protein present in two isoforms in humans, an adult-specific larger form (51 kDa) and an embryo-specific smaller form (32 kDa)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (He et al., 1999) describing AEBP2 isoforms.

claim: Both AEBP2 isoforms contain three Gli-Krüppel (Cys2-His2)-type zinc fingers.
source_text: both containing three Gli-Krüppel (Cys2-His2)-type zinc fingers
evidence_reasoning: This structural information is supported by citation (He et al., 1999).

claim: Atomic structures of the EED and RbAp48 subunits have been reported.
source_text: atomic structures of the EED and RbAp48 subunits have been reported
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations (Margueron et al., 2009; Nowak et al., 2011; Schmitges et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2010).

claim: The purified PRC2-AEBP2 complex has a molecular mass of approximately 275 kDa.
source_text: The molecular mass of the recombinant complex is ∼275 kDa.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly measured from size-exclusion chromatography experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Individual PRC2-AEBP2 particles have an elongated shape with a length of approximately 16 nm and a thickness of approximately 7 nm.
source_text: Individual particles have an elongated shape with a length of ∼16 nm and a thickness of ∼7 nm.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from negative-stain EM images shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Mild cross-linking with 0.015% glutaraldehyde improved the stability of the PRC2-AEBP2 complex for structural analysis.
source_text: comparison of class averages of the non cross-linked and the cross-linked sample (Figure 1D, bottom row), shows that the cross-linking had a positive effect on the stability of the complex, as judged by the increased detail in the class averages
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by comparing class averages from cross-linked and non-cross-linked samples in Figure 1D.

claim: The PRC2-AEBP2 complex consists of 4 different lobes (A, B, C, D), each about 55 Å in diameter, interconnected by two narrow arms.
source_text: The PRC2-AEBP2 complex consists of 4 different lobes, each about 55 Å in diameter (A, B, C, D), interconnected by two narrow arms (Arm 1, Arm 2).
evidence_reasoning: This structural description is based on the 3D EM reconstruction shown in Figure 4.

claim: The final resolution of the 3D reconstruction was estimated as 21 Å using the Fourier shell correlation criterion with a cutoff of 0.5.
source_text: Final resolution was estimated as 21 Å using the Fourier shell correlation criterion with a cutoff of 0.5.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct measurement from the resolution analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The WD40 domain of EED interacts with residues 40-68 of Ezh2.
source_text: Previous crystallographic analysis of the EED-Ezh2 complex described the interaction of the C-terminal WD40 propeller of EED with residues 40–68 of Ezh2
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to crystallographic studies (Han et al., 2007; Margueron et al., 2009).

claim: Cross-linking data shows that the peptide centered at residues K210/217/222 of Ezh2 binds the second SANT domain of Ezh2 at K510/514/515.
source_text: The peptide centered at residues [K210/217/222] binds the second SANT domain of Ezh2 [K510/514/515]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: AEBP2 region K118/121 interacts with the VEFS domain of Suz12 at K650.
source_text: associates with the VEFS domain of Suz12 [K650], and is also cross-linked to the same region of AEBP2 [K118/121]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5.

claim: AEBP2 binds to Ezh2's methyltransferase (SET)-containing C-terminus at residues K568-K740.
source_text: cross-linking data show that AEBP2 binds to Ezh2's methyltransferase (SET)-containing C-terminus [K568–K740]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: AEBP2 binds to Suz12's Zn finger domain at residues K414-K534.
source_text: as well as Suz12's Zn finger domain [K414–K534]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry data.

claim: The Zn finger domain of Suz12 at K465/468-K483 interacts with the methyltransferase domain of Ezh2 at K568-K740.
source_text: Furthermore, this region of Suz12 [K465/468–K483] also interacts with the methyltransferase domain of Ezh2 [K568–K740]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: The SET domain of Ezh2 and the Zn fingers of Suz12 and AEBP2 form a trimeric subcomplex.
source_text: suggesting a trimeric subcomplex that includes the SET domain of Ezh2 and the Zn fingers of Suz12 and AEBP2
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the cross-linking data showing interactions among these three domains.

claim: The N-terminal and C-terminal regions of Ezh2 are within proximity to, or directly interacting with each other.
source_text: we propose that these two terminal regions of Ezh2 are within proximity to, or directly interacting with each other
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from cross-linking data showing that both regions interact with the same domains of AEBP2 and Suz12.

claim: Crystal structures of the Drosophila Nurf55-Suz12 complex identified a small region of interaction between the WD40 domain of Nurf55 and an alpha helix of Suz12 (residues 77-93 in Drosophila, corresponding to 105-121 in human).
source_text: Two recently published crystal structures of the Drosophila Nurf55-Suz12 complex identified a small region of interaction between the WD40 domain of Nurf55 (an ortholog of RbAp48) and an alpha helix of Suz12 (residues 77–93, corresponding to 105–121 in human)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to crystal structure studies (Nowak et al., 2011; Schmitges et al., 2011).

claim: Internal cross-linking within the WD40 propeller of RbAp48 at K114/120-K160-K215/220 is consistent with the reported crystal structure of the isoform RbAp46.
source_text: We did identify internal cross-linking within the WD40 propeller of RbAp48 [K114/120–K160–K215/220], consistent with the reported crystal structure of the isoform RbAp46 (PDB: 3CFS; Figure 6B).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cross-linking data that matches the known crystal structure.

claim: The WD40 domain of RbAp48 at K307/309 interacts with the central portion of Suz12 at K167-K403.
source_text: we detect the presence of a set of three interactions between the WD40 domain of RbAp48 [K307/309] and the central portion of Suz12 [K167–K403]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry data.

claim: The central region of Suz12 at K304-K403 interacts with AEBP2 at K229-K274.
source_text: In addition to this interaction with RbAp48, we also observe cross-linking between this region of Suz12 [K304–K403] and AEBP2 [K229–K274].
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: AEBP2 residues K229-K274 interact with AEBP2's own Zn finger domain at K95-K166.
source_text: These residues of AEBP2 also interact with AEBP2's own Zn finger domain [K95–K166]
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from intra-molecular cross-linking data.

claim: RbAp48, the central domain of Suz12, and AEBP2 undergo extensive interactions.
source_text: Taken together, these findings suggest that RbAp48, the central domain of Suz12, and AEBP2 undergo extensive interactions
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the multiple cross-linking interactions observed among these components.

claim: AEBP2 plays a major role in coordinating different PRC2 subunits, explaining its stabilizing effect on the PRC2 complex.
source_text: we find that AEBP2 plays a major role in coordinating different PRC2 subunits, explaining its stabilizing effect on the PRC2 complex
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the extensive cross-linking data showing AEBP2 interactions with multiple PRC2 subunits.

claim: The EED WD40 domain is located at Lobe A of the PRC2-AEBP2 structure.
source_text: Comparing the internally GFP-tagged EED sample with the untagged form allowed us to identify the additional GFP density protruding from the WD40-shaped Lobe A
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of internally GFP-tagged EED constructs shown in Figure 7.

claim: The canonical histone H3-binding site is located in a cavity at the intersection of Lobe A and Arm 2.
source_text: This information, together with the crystal structure of histone H3-bound EED (Margueron et al., 2009), suggests that the canonical histone H3-binding site is located in a cavity at the intersection of Lobe A and Arm 2
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the localization of EED combined with the known crystal structure of histone H3-bound EED.

claim: The WD40 propeller of RbAp48 is located at Lobe D.
source_text: The GFP can be seen localizing to Lobe D, confirming that Suz12 interacts with the RbAp48 propeller at this position.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of Suz12-GFP123 construct shown in Figure 8.

claim: The first SANT domain of Ezh2 is positioned at the intersection of Lobe A and Arm 1.
source_text: The location of the GFP extra density suggests that the first SANT domain is positioned at the intersection of Lobe A and Arm 1
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of Ezh2-GFP303 construct shown in Figure 9.

claim: The second SANT domain of Ezh2 is positioned at the intersection of Arm 1 and Lobe B.
source_text: and the second at the intersection of Arm 1 and Lobe B
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of Ezh2-GFP436 construct shown in Figure 9.

claim: The proximity of the two SANT domains of Ezh2 is in very good agreement with cross-linking analysis.
source_text: The proximity of these two SANT domains is in very good agreement with our cross-linking analysis
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the consistency between EM localization data and cross-linking data.

claim: The methyltransferase SET domain of Ezh2 is located at Lobe B.
source_text: The methyltransferase SET domain of Ezh2 was located by reconstituting two complexes, one bearing an internal GFP tag immediately upstream of this domain (Ezh2-GFP594, Figure 9A, panel IV) and the other bearing a C-terminal GFP tag (Ezh2-GFP, Figure 9A, panel V). Both of these constructs localized to Lobe B
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of Ezh2-GFP594 and Ezh2-GFP constructs shown in Figure 9.

claim: Suz12's N-terminal region is located at Lobe C.
source_text: our labeling data suggest that Suz12's N-terminal region is located at Lobe C
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from EM analysis of Suz12-GFP269 construct shown in Figure 10.

claim: Suz12 terminates at Lobe B near the SET domain of Ezh2.
source_text: and terminates at Lobe B near the SET domain of Ezh2, most likely passing through Arm2
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from EM analysis of Suz12-ΔC-GFP construct combined with cross-linking data.

claim: The Zn finger domains of AEBP2 are located near Lobe A and Arm 1.
source_text: AEBP2-GFP84 (Figure 10A, panel III) and AEBP2-GFP115 (Figure 10A, panel IV) both localized near Lobe A and Arm 1.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of AEBP2-GFP84 and AEBP2-GFP115 constructs shown in Figure 10.

claim: The C-terminal region of AEBP2 is located between Lobes A and D, possibly within Arm 2.
source_text: 2D analysis of the AEBP2-EGFP–containing complex shows that the C-terminal region of AEBP2 is located between Lobes A and D, possibly within Arm 2
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from EM analysis of AEBP2-EGFP construct shown in Figure 10.

claim: AEBP2 runs in the opposite direction of Suz12, with its central portion located near Arm 1 and Lobe A, terminating near Arm 2 and the top of Lobe D.
source_text: Thus, AEBP2 runs in the opposite direction of Suz12, with its central portion located near Arm 1 and Lobe A, from where it continues along the PRC2 structure, terminating near Arm 2 and the top of Lobe D
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the combined EM localization data for multiple AEBP2 constructs.

claim: The PRC2-AEBP2 complex contains a single copy of each subunit.
source_text: Our labeling studies indicate that the PRC2-AEBP2 complex contains a single copy of each subunit, as we observed only one additional density within each of the individually tagged complexes.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation of only one tag density per tagged complex in EM analysis.

claim: The determined structure contains all the purified components.
source_text: These data also confirm that the determined structure contains all the purified components.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the successful localization of all subunits within the EM structure.

claim: The PRC2 subunit EED is able to bind the chromatin repressive mark H3K27me3 in trans via its WD40 domain, thus enhancing PRC2 mediated methylation of H3K27 in oligonucleosomes.
source_text: Previous reports have shown that the PRC2 subunit EED is able to bind the chromatin repressive mark H3K27me3 in trans, via its WD40 domain, thus enhancing PRC2 mediated methylation of H3K27 in oligonucleosomes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies (Margueron et al., 2009; Xu et al., 2010).

claim: EED-mediated activation results in propagation of the repressive chromatin state to neighboring nucleosomes containing newly incorporated unmodified histone H3.
source_text: This activation results in propagation of the repressive chromatin state to neighboring nucleosomes containing newly incorporated unmodified histone H3
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Hansen et al., 2008; Margueron et al., 2009).

claim: Binding of the chromatin activation marks H3K4me3 and H3K36me2-3 inhibits PRC2 activity if placed in cis on the same tail containing the target lysine H3K27.
source_text: the studies of Schmitges and colleagues suggested that binding of the chromatin activation marks H3K4me3 and H3K36me2-3, inhibits PRC2 activity if placed in cis on the same tail containing the target lysine H3K27
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Schmitges et al., 2011.

claim: The subunit Suz12, and in particular its VEFS domain, is responsible for mediating the inhibition of PRC2 by H3K4me3 and H3K36me2-3.
source_text: it has been proposed that the subunit Suz12, and in particular its VEFS domain, is responsible in mediating this inhibition
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Schmitges et al., 2011.

claim: The inhibitory effect of H3K4me3 and H3K36me2-3 can be reversed by the addition of H3K27me3 containing peptides.
source_text: Since this inhibitory effect can be reversed by the addition of H3K27me3 containing peptides
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Schmitges et al., 2011.

claim: PRC2 can simultaneously integrate inhibitory and activating chromatin marks, tuning its enzymatic activity based on the surrounding chromatin state.
source_text: it has been thought that PRC2 can simultaneously integrate inhibitory and activating chromatin marks tuning its enzymatic activity based on the surrounding chromatin state
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Schmitges et al., 2011.

claim: The Ezh2 methyltransferase domain forms a structural core with the WD40 domain of EED and the VEFS domain of Suz12.
source_text: Our structure shows that the Ezh2's methyltransferase domain forms a structural core with the two activity-controlling elements of PRC2, the WD40 domain of EED and the VEFS domain of Suz12
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from the 3D EM structure and subunit localization data.

claim: The regulatory mechanisms of EED and Suz12 on PRC2 activity could be structurally supported by their physical interaction with the SET domain.
source_text: This suggests that the proposed regulatory mechanisms of these domains on PRC2 activity could be structurally supported by their physical interaction with the SET domain.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the structural proximity of these domains observed in the EM structure.

claim: SANT domains have been shown to be important in coupling histone-tail binding to enzymatic activity in many chromatin regulating complexes.
source_text: SANT domains have been shown to be important in coupling histone-tail binding to enzymatic activity in many chromatin regulating complexes
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Boyer et al., 2004; Nowak et al., 2011).

claim: The two SANT domains of Ezh2 are positioned between the EED WD40 domain and the SET domain.
source_text: the two SANT domains of Ezh2 are positioned between the EED WD40 domain and the SET domain
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from the subunit localization data shown in the EM structure.

claim: The position of SANT domains suggests they could play a role in transmitting the H3K27me3 binding signal from EED to the Ezh2 SET domain.
source_text: suggesting that they could play a role in transmitting the H3K27me3 binding signal from EED to the Ezh2 SET domain
evidence_reasoning: This is speculated based on the structural positioning of these domains and known SANT domain functions.

claim: The VEFS domain of Suz12 and the SANT and SET domains of Ezh2 together interact with two Zn fingers from AEBP2 and Suz12.
source_text: At the opposite end of the core module, the VEFS domain of Suz12 and the SANT and SET domains of Ezh2 together interact with two Zn fingers from AEBP2 and Suz12
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cross-linking data and structural localization.

claim: The position of the Suz12 VEFS domain with respect to the Ezh2 SET domain suggests how the H3K4me3 and H3K36me2/3 inhibition via Suz12 could be transferred to Ezh2.
source_text: The position of the Suz12 VEFS domain with respect to the Ezh2 SET domain suggests how the H3K4me3 and H3K36me2/3 inhibition via Suz12 could be transferred to Ezh2, regulating its methyltransferase activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculated based on the structural positioning of these domains.

claim: The close proximity of the VEFS and SET domains could explain why the gene activation marks need to be on the tail being modified in order to block methyltransferase activity.
source_text: The close proximity of these elements could also explain why the gene activation marks need to be on the tail being modified in order to block methyltransferase activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculated based on the structural proximity observed in the EM structure.

claim: When chromatin domains are targeted for repression, PRC2 is recruited to deposit the repressive H3K27me3 histone mark at nucleosome-associated regions of DNA.
source_text: when chromatin domains are targeted for repression, PRC2 is recruited to deposit the repressive H3K27me3 histone mark at nucleosome-associated regions of DNA
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge about PRC2 function, consistent with cited literature.

claim: Existing H3K27me3 marks are recognized by EED and, possibly in cooperation with Ezh2's SANT domains, Ezh2 methyltransferase activity is increased.
source_text: Existing H3K27me3 marks are recognized by EED and, possibly in cooperation with Ezh2's SANT domains, Ezh2 methyltransferase activity is increased
evidence_reasoning: This combines established knowledge from citations with speculation about SANT domain involvement based on structural data.

claim: When PRC2 comes into contact with the boundary of an active gene, the interaction between H3K4me3, H3K36me2, and H3K36me3 with the VEFS domain of Suz12 could be propagated to the Ezh2 subunit, blocking PRC2 activity.
source_text: When PRC2 comes into contact with the boundary of an active gene, the interaction between H3K4me3, H3K36me2, and H3K36me3 with the VEFS domain of Suz12, could be propagated to the Ezh2 subunit, blocking PRC2 activity
evidence_reasoning: This combines established knowledge from citations with speculation about the mechanism based on structural data.

claim: PRC2 favors di- and oligonucleosome substrates over mononucleosomes, octamers, or histone H3 peptides.
source_text: Previous studies have shown that PRC2 favors di- and oligonucleosome substrates over mononucleosomes, octamers, or histone H3 peptides
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies (Cao and Zhang, 2004a; Margueron et al., 2008).

claim: The two WD40 domains of EED and RbAp48 are located at opposite ends of the PRC2 structure.
source_text: The two WD40 domains of EED and RbAp48 (indicated in blue) are located at opposite ends.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed from the 3D EM structure and subunit localization shown in Figure 4.

claim: The distance between the two WD40 domains is approximately 100 Å.
source_text: The distance between the two WD40 domains is ∼100 Å
evidence_reasoning: This is measured from the 3D EM structure.

claim: The distance of approximately 100 Å between the two WD40 domains is consistent with the length of a histone H3 tail.
source_text: consistent with the length of a histone H3 tail
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred by comparing the measured distance with known histone H3 tail length.

claim: The molecular architecture described for human PRC2 is expected to be conserved throughout higher eukaryotes due to sequence similarity between PRC2 components from different species.
source_text: Given the similarity in sequence between PRC2 components from different species, we expect the molecular architecture that we described for human PRC2 to be conserved throughout higher eukaryotes.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from known sequence conservation of PRC2 components across species.

claim: The structure provides an invaluable structural context to understand previous biochemical data on PRC2.
source_text: the human PRC2 structure presented here provides us with the first full picture of the molecular organization of this fundamental complex and offers an invaluable structural context to understand previous biochemical data
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary statement supported by the integration of structural data with previous biochemical findings throughout the manuscript.

claim: The functional mapping of different activities within the physical shape of the complex leads to novel, testable hypotheses on how PRC2 interacts with chromatin.
source_text: Furthermore, the functional mapping of different activities within the physical shape of the complex leads to novel, testable hypotheses on how PRC2 interacts with chromatin that should inspire future research of PRC2 function and regulation.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the integration of structural and functional data to generate mechanistic hypotheses.
